clue.text: A case of smog, say

definitions.meaning: a large travelling bag that opens into two hinged halves
smog blends smoke and fog into one word, the type example of a blend word

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a two-part travelling trunk and a blend word such as smog, which fuses smoke and fog.

clue.text: Oscar scarpered, starting to go ape

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
scarpered is British slang for ran away, so RAN

indicators.note: starting to points at the opening letter of the next word, go

explanation.surface: Someone called Oscar bolted and then began behaving like an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form of orang-utan, the great ape of Borneo and Sumatra.

clue.text: Censure counter-revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around or overthrown, so the letters of counter are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political denunciation of those opposing a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter-revolutionary' reads as one hyphenated word; split it, and 'revolutionary' churns the letters of COUNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone can mean to rebuke or criticise them severely, as well as to beat them.

clue.text: A new melody that's developed without end for the choir to perform

definitions.note: a phrase describing a piece of choral music, standing for the noun

indicators.note: without end tells us to drop the final letter of the word

parts.note: in music a theme is the melody a composer develops through a piece

explanation.surface: A composer works up a fresh tune, unfinished, for a choir to sing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' drops the last E of THEME to leave THEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral composition, typically sung in church, is the classic thing a choir performs.

clue.text: Number addressing the beach, once

parts.note: thou is the old second-person pronoun once used when addressing someone; 'once' in the clue flags the archaism
sand is what a beach is made of, standing for the beach itself

explanation.surface: Speaking to the seaside in some old-fashioned way, a figure is announced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks THOU as archaic: the old way of addressing someone, as in 'thou, sand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal figure, ten hundreds.

clue.text: On the left in Mâcon, also in Mainz, in time

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits within another here, the German placed inside the time word

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Mainz is a German city, and the German word for also is auch

explanation.surface: A traveller notes directions in a French town and a German one.
explanation.walkthrough: Mâcon is in France, so the definition is French for 'on the left'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase for leftwards or on the left-hand side, as said in a French town.

clue.text: Cheated, having made a return Dover-Calais trip

definitions.meaning: betrayed someone by working against them while appearing to help

definitions.text: having made a return Dover-Calais trip
definitions.meaning: a round trip from Dover to Calais means passing over the Channel twice

explanation.walkthrough: Dover and Calais are the English and French ports on either side of the Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayed by a supposed ally; also, read literally, having gone over the water two times.

clue.text: Accommodation always in arena

indicators.note: in places the poetic word inside the arena word

parts.note: a stage is an arena or scene of action
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A venue that always has rooms available inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheapest passenger quarters on a ship, so a kind of lodging aboard.

clue.text: Abbot is a terribly rich fellow and terribly tired

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of rich are jumbled

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: terribly again signals a jumble, this time of the letters of tired

explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges RICH into RCHI and TIRED into DRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior cleric in the Orthodox Church, the head of a large monastery, equivalent to an abbot.

clue.text: Goat wandering round NZ region

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so the letters of Goat move

parts.note: a round shape is a ring, the letter O

explanation.surface: A goat roams around a part of New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: A region in the south of New Zealand's South Island, home to Dunedin.

clue.text: A God-and-Mammon sort of sailing boat?

definitions.text: A God-and-Mammon sort of sailing boat?

parts.words: A God-and-Mammon sort of sailing boat?
parts.note: a vessel with a pair of masts fits the phrase

explanation.walkthrough: Mammon is wealth personified; Matthew's Gospel warns you cannot serve both God and Mammon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel with two masts, punningly a servant of two lords.

clue.text: Are they learning to be cotton-processors?

definitions.text: Are they learning to be cotton-processors?

parts.words: Are they learning to be cotton-processors?
parts.note: novices are learning; split, the word reads 'be' plus machine operators who separate cotton from seed

explanation.walkthrough: A cotton gin separates fibre from seeds; those who run one are ginners.

clue.text: East European restraint is suggested

indicators.note: is suggested means the sound of the restraint word hints at the answer

parts.note: a check is a restraint or curb

explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Czech Republic, in central-eastern Europe.

clue.text: Badge from old car firm in same French review

indicators.note: in places the car firm inside the French word
review is read as re-view, looking back, so the French word runs backwards

parts.note: même is the French word for same
BL was British Leyland, the former British car maker

explanation.surface: A badge produced by a former motor company, written up in a French magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a symbol or badge representing a group or idea.

clue.text: Such plans may affect tables, just the same

indicators.note: may affect suggests the word tables is altered, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: id is short for idem, Latin for the same, used in references

explanation.surface: Certain plans could change the timetables all the same.
explanation.walkthrough: From Burns: 'The best-laid schemes o' mice an' men gang aft agley'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans made with the greatest care, which proverbially go wrong anyway.

clue.text: Style of bowling causing murder an' turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is a state of confusion, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A bowling style that provokes violent chaos on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowling is overarm; bowling with the hand below the shoulder is a quaint or forbidden style.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivering a ball with the arm swung below shoulder height, a bowling technique.

clue.text: Cow, large 20 eating imitative bird

indicators.note: eating means one word swallows the other, the bird going inside

parts.note: 20 points to the answer at 20 across; a runt is a large breed of that domestic bird
the mina (or myna) is a talking bird that mimics speech

explanation.surface: A cow, a big bird and a mimic in some farmyard scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow is an example of a cud-chewing animal.

clue.text: Jam-packed?

parts.note: traffic jams pack the roads at the busiest commuting time of day

explanation.definitionFit: The peak commuting period, when roads are full of traffic jams.

clue.text: In a Channel island love is valour

indicators.note: In places love and is inside the island's name

parts.note: Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, near Guernsey
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: On a Channel island, love is a form of bravery.
explanation.definitionFit: Great courage or bravery; synonyms.

clue.text: Gull. Yes and no!

parts.note: a gull is a dupe, and so is this word; yet as a bird a gull is not this bird

explanation.walkthrough: Both words mean a dupe, someone easily fooled, but the birds differ: hence yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: Both can mean a dupe or easily swindled person, though as birds they are different.

clue.text: Suppose there's silver in one source of gold!

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the silver symbol within the mine

parts.note: gold is dug from a mine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Imagine finding silver in a gold mine!

clue.text: Remove obstacle in river

indicators.note: in places the obstacle within the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
a let is an old word for a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

clue.text: Spanish composer cutting sherry production

indicators.note: cutting means docking the word, removing its tail letter

parts.note: the solera is the tiered barrel system used to age and blend sherry

explanation.surface: A Spanish musician slashing output of a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting' drops the final A of SOLERA.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Soler was an 18th-century Catalan composer of keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: European rice ruined by invading antelope

indicators.note: invading means the antelope pushes into the scrambled rice
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of rice are scrambled

parts.note: the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A European's crop is wrecked by antelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' looks too vague to define anything; here it is the definition, a native of one northern island nation. 'ruined' scrambles the grain to ICER before the antelope goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Iceland is a northern European.

clue.text: Stoop during parade, ignominiously

indicators.note: during means within the span of the following words, whose letters hold the answer

explanation.surface: Bowing during a parade in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: To condescend to do something beneath one's dignity, as stooping does figuratively.

clue.text: Cut out damaged main in the establishment

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the establishment word

parts.note: the elite are the ruling establishment

indicators.note: damaged means broken, so the letters of main are jumbled

explanation.surface: A damaged water main in a building has to be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the establishment' reads as a building in the surface but means the ruling class. 'damaged' turns the pipe word into MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove or exclude completely, a synonym for excise.

clue.text: Fool muddling addition and subtraction!

indicators.note: muddling means confusing the order of the letters
subtraction tells us to take away the letters of 'and' from addition before mixing

explanation.surface: Only a fool would confuse adding up with taking away!
explanation.walkthrough: Remove A, N, D from ADDITION to leave DITIO, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid person, a simpleton; synonyms.

clue.text: Small fragments there in appearance on board

indicators.note: on board signals being inside the ship letters

parts.note: on board means aboard ship, and SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: in places there inside the appearance word

parts.note: mien is a person's look or appearance

explanation.surface: Tiny shards appearing there on the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SS (steamship) is the conventional ship; 'on board' puts MITHEREEN inside it.
